PanoRef coverage optimizer review and follow-up work.

Current state:
- Latest head adds 17 coverage-engine files, a worker, UI, and tests. Joint mode genuinely evaluates candidate pairs rather than greedy first-origin selection.
- Verdict from prior review: algorithm architecture 8/10, search-mode correctness 7.5/10, readiness for complex imported sets 4/10. Promising, not production-ready.
- What is right: deterministic area-weighted triangle sampling via barycentric coords; origin evaluation includes segment occlusion, geometric face normals, viewing angle, approximate projected texel density, separate visibility/usable-coverage bitsets, continuous quality; joint mode ranks by bitset union then applies quality/contribution tie-breakers; shared coarse-to-fine engine organized as 4096 coarse, 256 candidates, retained pair seeds, 24576 fine, local offsets, separate fixed-first and joint branches; tests cover deterministic sampling, double-sided occlusion, marginal second-origin ranking, non-greedy pair ranking, candidate generation, both search modes.

Blockers identified:
1. Imported sets can produce zero legal candidates. Non-floor objects store entire AABB as obstacle; clearance is distance from origin to AABB, points inside get zero and are rejected. A single imported SceneObject whose AABB encloses the whole room can reject every sensible origin. Fix: use actual geometry clearance (point-to-triangle distance, sphere intersection, or shapecast) via coverage BVH; obstacle bounds should be per connected mesh/cluster, not per imported object. Add regression test with one imported object containing floor, walls, empty interior.
2. Geometry representation will not scale to heavy imports. Every triangle expanded into three independent Vec3 arrays + normal array + IDs + area; for 3M triangles packed minimum ~144MB, actual JS objects/arrays/64-bit numbers several times larger, then structured-cloned into worker. BVH recursively sorts/slices JS index arrays; triangle intersection allocates temporary 3-element arrays, extreme GC pressure on millions of raycasts. Fix: compact typed arrays (positions Float32Array, indices Uint32Array, normals?, meshRanges Uint32Array, transforms Float32Array), transfer ArrayBuffers instead of cloning nested objects; for BVH use three-mesh-bvh, flat typed-array BVH with in-place partitioning, or per-mesh BVHs; avoid expanding indexed vertices into three world-space vertex arrays per triangle.
3. Geometry extraction still blocks main thread. Panel synchronously calls extractCoverageScene(project) before creating/posting to worker, so scene recreation, triangle flattening, world-transform application, geometry disposal, structured cloning all block UI. Fix: move extraction into worker or chunk it and yield between meshes.
4. "Apply to selected panorama pair" is conceptually wrong. Workspace handler writes optimized origins directly into existing panorama references via updatePanoReference(..., { origin }). Changing metadata does not transform the image; it projects old pixels from wrong point, ruining alignment. Correct workflow: fixed-first preserve existing panorama/origin, move next capture origin to B, render new graybox panorama, inpaint/generate styled panorama, import as secondary, associate with actual origin; joint mode create two-origin capture plan, move to A, capture/render A, move to B, capture/render B, associate each with its actual origin. Do not rewrite origins of already captured panoramas.
5. Reachable upper bound mathematically inconsistent. reachableCoverage uses coarse sample bank + all coarse candidates; final combined coverage uses different fine sample bank generated with seed+1; both placed in same result and used for reachable efficiency, so UI can show combined 83%, reachable upper bound 80%, reachable captured 100%. Clamp hides impossible ratio but does not repair incompatible estimates. Also fixed-first reachable set calculated before arbitrary first origin evaluated, so fixed first origin not included in reachable upper bound at all. Fix: use common validation sample bank for final pair coverage, reachable candidate union, efficiency; for fixed-first include fixed origin in reachable union. Separate coarse/fine search banks internally OK, but reported metrics must be evaluated on one shared final bank.
6. Fixed-first does not enforce minimum separation. Joint mode rejects pairs below minimumOriginSeparation; fixed-first rankSecondOrigins only filters by object identity, not position/distance, so even identical candidate position can survive. Add distance(first.position, candidate.position) >= minimumOriginSeparation.
7. "Four-level refinement" not truly iterative. For every seed all offsets generated around original seed (seed ± spacing/2, ± spacing/4, ± spacing/8, ± spacing/16); does not select best half-step result and center quarter-step search around new result. Useful multiresolution neighborhood sample but not the coordinate/pattern refinement described in plan; true refinement loop would update center after every level.
8. Local candidates can float between floors. Candidate validation only checks whether a floor exists somewhere below candidate; local offsets retain original Y; on sloped terrain or multilevel sets offset can move over lower floor while preserving upper floor camera height, leaving origin floating meters above new floor. Fix per offset: find floor under new X/Z, set Y = floorY + panoramaHeightMeters, then perform clearance.
9. Optimizer and runtime renderer use different quality rules. Optimizer evaluates angle and texel density; when both panoramas visible, actual shader still blends only by distance, so optimizer may prefer source for frontal angle while runtime favors closer but more grazing source; optimized coverage result and visible result do not fully agree. Shader should use same approximate quality function and preferably winner-takes-most selection rather than broad continuous averaging.

Recent work in this window:
- Reviewed projectedStyleMaterials.ts around projectedQualityAt and blend logic; shader already uses continuous visibility scores, projectedQualityAt with angleQuality * resolutionQuality, blend modes, winner-takes-most via pow(score,4), primary/secondary dominance 1.15 for modes 2/3.
- Patched multiOriginInteraction.test.ts: removed stale test guarding old distance-only blend heuristic (PROJECTED_FALLOFF = 6.0, projectedConfidence); replaced with assertion protecting new optimizer-aligned angle/texel-quality selection and dominance modes (projectedQualityAt, projectedBlendMode == 2 ? 1.15 : 1.0, projectedBlendMode == 3 ? 1.15 : 1.0, not.toContain('projectedConfidence')).
- Ran targeted test: tests/multiOriginInteraction.test.ts 36 tests passed.
- Ran full suite: 42 test files, 371 tests passed; notable long tests: projectionCoverage.test.ts 10 tests 39235ms (runs both complete optimizer modes on 100k+ triangle indexed fixture), occlusion/projected compile/receive tests ~4s each with real WebGL pixel readback. Lint (tsc --noEmit) and build (vite build) both passed.

User directive:
- Rebase onto main and resolve PR conflict.
- Add allowed-floor-region mechanism or robust imported-floor component filtering.
- Run one real complex imported-set benchmark and add full 100K+ optimizer integration test, not merely BVH-construction test.
- Set goal to accomplish above, then spawn subagent whose job is to disprove goal is fully complete; have it report what still lacks; fix that; repeat until subagent unable to find holes.

Open issues / continuation constraints:
- Blockers 1–9 above still need addressing; only blocker 9 partially addressed via shader/test alignment so far.
- No GitHub Actions workflow runs attached to latest head, so reported test suite not independently enforced in CI.
- Must not invent facts; preserve current task intent and constraints.
